mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Domestic tax authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction of tax residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or equivalent corporate registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney granted in favor of the Spanish incorporation representative or notary, including Spanish certified translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the grantor's jurisdiction, authenticated by apostille or consular legalization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; otherwise consular legalization, followed by official Spanish translation by a sworn translator-traductor jurado

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and beneficial owners against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (EU Regulation 269/2014 and 881/2002), UN Security Council sanctions lists including Resolutions 1267, 1989, 2253, and 2368, the OFAC SDN List, UK HMT consolidated sanctions, and Spanish domestic counter-terrorism financing lists administered by SEPBLAC and the Comisión de Vigilancia de Actividades de Financiación del Terrorismo. Politically Exposed Persons must be identified in accordance with Article 14 of Ley 10/2010, including domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates. Enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and source-of-wealth/source-of-funds verification are mandatory for any PEP, sanctions-hit, or adverse-media flag; the filing of the UBO declaration with the Registro Central de Titularidades Reales is a precondition to inscription of the company in the Registro Mercantil.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) online denomination certification service operated by the Colegio de Registradores de España, accessible via https://www.registradores.org and the RMC electronic portal for 'Certificación de Denominación Social' (negative certification of company name).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate denominations must be expressed in Latin script; any non-Latin alphabet must be transliterated phonetically into the Spanish alphabet. The name may be in Spanish or in a foreign language with Spanish orthography and accentuation, provided it is not contrary to Spanish law, morality, or public order. The obligatory suffix 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.' must be included. Denominations must not be identical or phonetically or semantically confusingly similar to any existing registered company under Articles 143-149 of the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España, Estado, Gobierno, Nacional, Ministerio, Administración, Comunidad Autónoma, Ayuntamiento and similar references to sovereign or public institutions (require prior authorization from the Consejo de Ministros or the relevant competent authority)

Banco, Caja, Caja de Ahorros, Entidad de Crédito, Seguro, Reaseguro, Aseguradora, Correduría de Seguros and other regulated financial or insurance terms (reserved for entities holding administrative license from the Banco de España or Dirección General de Seguros y Fondos de Pensiones)
Sociedad Anónima, S.A., S.L., S.Coop. and other legal form tokens inconsistent with the true corporate form or likely to mislead as to liability regime
Nombres de personas físicas without express written consent of the person involved
Expressions contrary to law, public order, morality, or good customs, and denominations that suggest official accreditation, state guarantee, or public service status
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the denomination is rejected, the applicant may file a new application for an alternative proposed name or challenge the refusal. A formal administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) may be lodged before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública of the Ministerio de Justicia within one month of notification, pursuant to Ley 39/2015, de 1 de octubre, del Procedimiento Administrativo Común. If the administrative appeal is dismissed, the applicant may file a contentious-administrative appeal (recurso contencioso-administrativo) before the relevant court within two months. In parallel, registry qualification challenges may be raised under Articles 322-327 of the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil. Practical recommendation: secure a secondary denomination certificate at the outset and present Plan A and Plan B names in the incorporation deed to avoid re-filing delays.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or serviced office is acceptable for registration of the registered office address where mail receipt and administrative dispatch are verifiable, but the place of effective management must be in Spain for corporate tax residence under Article 8 of Ley 27/2014, de 27 de noviembre, del Impuesto sobre Sociedades. For a marine insurance surveying business in ISIC 5222, a pure virtual letterbox without a local operational address creates substance risk in tax audits and is commercially inadvisable because survey records, claims files, client interviews, and underwriting deliverables require a verifiable physical or brached operational presence. A fractional serviced office or warehousing-adjacent survey office is the recommended structure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk, estimated below 15% annual probability of an unannounced on-site visit from the Agencia Tributaria during a corporate tax audit and a negligible probability of SEPBLAC AML inspection because a marine surveyor is not a listed obliged entity under Article 2 of Ley 10/2010 unless it also performs insurance intermediation. Ship registries and underwriters conducting claims audits may perform contractual site inspections, which raises the operational probability for marine insurance surveyor premises to approximately 25% during the first year of active claim handling.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registro Mercantil Central negative denomination certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Colegio de Registradores de España)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RMC tariff, approximately EUR 18-25 per certificate application

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial fee for execution of incorporation deed (escritura de constitución) and articles of association (estatutos sociales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Notary (Notario del Colegio Notarial, generally of Madrid or the incorporation city)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff scale under Real Decreto 1426/1989, as amended; EUR 300-600 for a standard SL deed with EUR 3,000 capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registro Mercantil Provincial inscription tariff for first registration of the company and of the directors/governing body
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial corresponding to the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff approved by the Ministerio de Justicia (arancel registral), EUR 80-150 for standard SL incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille legalization of foreign shareholder, tax residence, passport, and power-of-attorney documents (approximately 4-6 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Apostille authority of each origin state plus Spanish Consulate where consular legalization applies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document apostille and consular fee schedule of the issuing country; market benchmark USD 20-30 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of foreign public and corporate documents by sworn translator (traductor jurado)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator appointed by the Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores / traductor jurado
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 150-250 per document set

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee and administrative processing fee; market benchmark EUR 15-70 per person

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Application and accreditation dossier for statutory marine insurance surveying license/habilitation (perito o comisario de averías habilitado for marine claims surveying under maritime insurance regulatory requirements)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de la Marina Mercante and/or Dirección General de Seguros y Fondos de Pensiones, as applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative fee where published; otherwise market benchmark for professional accreditation documentation, EUR 50-150

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence, UBO piercing analysis, drafting of articles of association, and closing legal opinion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish qualified attorney (abogado in practice) and, if required, registered tax advisor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for an SL incorporation with international shareholders; EUR 800-1,500 fixed fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), as amended by Law 18/2022, Articles 19-28 (public deed, registration and pre-incorporation contracts), Article 4 (minimum share capital), Article 58 (registered office), Articles 209-210 (administrators) and Articles 233 et seq. (shareholder resolutions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for the negative name certificate; Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office for registration of the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) recorded in the Mercantile Register; submitted by the notary through the Single Electronic Registry to the Registro Mercantil Provincial.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Standard SL: minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid up at incorporation; cash payments must be deposited in a blocked bank account in Spain until registration. Under Law 18/2022, an SL en formación sucesiva may be incorporated with less than EUR 3,000 but not less than EUR 1 fully paid; the company must disclose this status and irreversibly commit to reaching EUR 3,000 within five years.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the founding meeting of [Company Name] (the 'Company') held in [City], Spain, the founding members unanimously pass the following resolutions: (1) The share subscriptions stated in the deed of incorporation are ratified, and each subscriber shall pay the subscribed amount into the Company's restricted cash account at [Bank], as required by law. (2) The registered office is fixed at [Street, Postal Code, City], Province of [Province], and all legal notices shall be served there. (3) [Full Name] is appointed sole Administrator of the Company for an indefinite term, with the broad powers enumerated in the articles of association. (4) The Administrator is authorized to execute every step necessary for registration, tax activation, and licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Madrid (online through the electronic registry service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the denomination certification application with three proposed corporate names. The registry confirms that none of the names is identical or confusingly similar to an existing company. The resulting negative name certificate is valid for three months and must be attached to the public deed.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each founding member
List of three proposed names in order of preference
Proof of payment of the official registry fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first name is rejected, the registry automatically considers the second and third alternatives; if all conflict, file a new application with other names before the certificate expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Company-in-Formation Cash Escrow Account and Deposit Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution authorized by the Banco de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a current account in the name of the company in formation and deposit the subscribed capital in cash or by transfer. Obtain an irrevocable bank certificate stating the subscriber, amount and account number, proving that the capital is unavailable until the company's registration in the Mercantile Registry.
required_dossiers: Identification and NIE of each subscriber
Statement signed by founders designating the account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the credit institution declines the account, choose another bank or require the notary to execute a personal-responsibility guarantee for deferred cash payment; if the certificate contains defects, ask the bank to reissue it within the statutory two-month tender period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Public Incorporation Deed before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary (Notario) in the locality of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend the notarial meeting with the final articles of association. The notary verifies the legal capacity of the subscribers, the legality of the bylaws and the capital deposit, reads the deed, receives signatures and issues certified copies. The notary then submits the deed electronically to the Mercantile Registry.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate dated within the last 3 months
NIF certificates or tax identification of the founding persons, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to authorize due to defects, amend the bylaws or supply missing evidence and reconvene; a notarial protest may be filed against unreasonable refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Deed in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary transmits the public deed and required supporting documents to the Registrar. The Registrar examines legal conformity and issues a provisional or definitive registration. The company acquires full legal personality upon registration. Obtain a registration certificate to be used in tax and licensing filings.
required_dossiers: Certificate of no prior tax debts for founders where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar opposes registration with a 'defect' notice, remedy the noted defect through a corrective public deed and resubmit; if the defect is legal interpretation, it may be appealed before the Directorate General of Legal Security and Public Faith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification Number, Register with AEAT and Secure Municipal Activity License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and the city council (Ayuntamiento) of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, file Model 036 with AEAT to obtain the definitive NIF, register for corporate income tax and, where applicable, the Spanish Economic Activities Tax (IAE). Concurrently submit the municipal activity declaration or prior communication to the city council for the premises. Finally, register the company with social security if hiring employees.
required_dossiers: Occupational health and fire safety documentation for the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT detects inconsistent data, file a rectification Model 036 with the deed and registry certificate; if the municipality requires a stricter license, obtain an architectural report and technical measurements, or change the premises to a zoning-compliant office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General de Seguros y Fondos de Pensiones (DGSFP), Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business, for the claims-surveyor registration; Dirección General de Marina Mercante, Ministry of Transport and Sustainable Mobility, for vessel surveyor accreditation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Administrative registration as 'Perito de Seguros' (insurance claims surveyor) in the DGSFP Registry, together with 'Perito Naval' accreditation when the activity includes physical inspection of vessel hulls and marine cargo.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and Demographic Challenge (MITECO), through the competent environmental authority (Consejería de Medio Ambiente) of the relevant Autonomous Community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA for office-based surveying; only a municipal environmental communication (comunicación ambiental) is required, plus registration as a small waste producer if lubricants, reagents or survey chemicals are used on site.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Waste handling under Law 7/2022 on waste and contaminated soils and Royal Decree 1055/2022 on packaging; ship-sourced discharges, where a survey boat is operated, must meet MARPOL Annex I (oil), Annex IV (sewage) and Annex V (garbage), and port reception facilities must be used under Royal Decree 159/2022; refrigerants from air-conditioning units must comply with Regulation 517/2014/EU.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and first-occupancy license for the registered office (licencia de primera ocupación); local civil defense (Protección Civil) inspection if the premises are publicly accessible; structural load verification by a competent technician if heavy inspection equipment is stored; and occupational safety implementation under Law 31/1995, including a port/shipboard access protocol for marine survey work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), statutory agency of the Ministerio de Hacienda. Electronic portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; SII web services and TEU notifications available via the same portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Spanish SL: (1) Apply for provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) through AEAT before executing the notarial incorporation deed, normally filed by the notary; (2) Execute the public deed before a Spanish Notary; (3) File Form 036 (declaración censal) with AEAT within one month of incorporation to activate the tax census and, simultaneously, VAT registration for the intended economic activity; (4) Register the company in the Registro Mercantil, converting the provisional NIF into the definitive NIF/CIF (código de identificación fiscal); (5) Request the definitive tax ID via Form 036 after registry registration; (6) Obtain an electronic X.509 certificate (FNMT-RCM or corporate certificate) to comply with mandatory electronic filing for VAT, corporate income tax, and SII records. A non-resident foreign entity contracting the SL requires no Spanish VAT ID but, if it makes supplies in Spain, must obtain a NIF for non-resident entities through a tax representative under Article 86 RD 1065/2007; the SL itself, as a resident company, acts as a fully registered domestic VAT taxpayer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. An SL is a resident entity under Article 8 Ley 27/2014 (LIS) and is taxed on worldwide income under Impuesto sobre Sociedades at the standard 25% rate; newly created SLs engaged in economic activity pay 15% on taxable profits of the first two years (Art. 29.1 LIS). Territorial_Scope: Worldwside taxation with ordinary and indirect foreign tax credits (Art. 31-32 LIS). Tax_Exempt_Zone: Not automatically applicable; the Canary Islands Special Zone (ZEC) offers a 4% CIT rate but requires prior authorization, minimum investment, and job creation; absent ZEC authorization, the standard regime applies. No pass-through classification is available for an SL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not recognize US-style check-the-box elections; entity classification follows corporate law form and the European accounting directives. Available elections include: (1) optional tax consolidation regime (Arts. 61-71 LIS) for a group of companies with ≥75% direct/indirect control, applied uniformly and irrevocable for one taxation period; (2) option for the ZEC special regime in the Canary Islands (4% corporate rate) subject to prior administrative authorization; (3) accelerated depreciation of new tangible fixed assets (Art. 103 LIS) and reduced depreciation options for SMEs (Art. 102 LIS); (4) choice between the foreign tax credit and deductible foreign tax expense under Art. 31 LIS; (5) VAT general regime versus the simplified regime (Régimen Simplificado) for qualifying small businesses, elected in Form 036; (6) ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules (transposed by Law 11/2021) are mandatory, with no elective neutralization mechanism except the taxpayer's proof of inclusion in both jurisdictions, and the 'tax transparency' optional treatment under Art. 100 LIS for Spanish entities owned by non-residents is available only for certain collective investment vehicles, not for an SL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido), Ley 37/1992, Royal Decree 1624/1992, and EU Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic-turnover exemption threshold applies under the standard Spanish VAT regime; any entrepreneur or professional effecting taxable supplies in Spanish territory must register before the first supply, regardless of annual amount. The simplified regime applies only to activities listed in the annex to Royal Decree 1624/1992 and is conditioned on the prior-year volume of operations net of VAT not exceeding EUR 250,000 and purchases not exceeding EUR 250,000. For non-established foreign suppliers, VAT registration in Spain is required before the first taxable event (no threshold). The real-time SII reporting threshold is EUR 6,000,000 annual turnover; e-invoicing law (Ley 18/2022) foresees a EUR 8,000,000 threshold for accelerated B2B e-invoicing compliance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2G: E-invoices in Facturae 3.2 XML must be submitted to the General Point of Entry for Electronic Invoices (FACE) since 15 January 2015, mandatory for all suppliers to the Spanish public sector. Real-time clearance: the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) requires large taxpayers (turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000), VAT-group members, and companies under the simplified/ equivalent regimes to submit records of issued and received invoices to AEAT through API/web services within 4 calendar days of the record date, extended to 8 calendar days for transaction windows set by AEAT (e.g., December); records are transmitted in XML (Criterios de registro SII) and certified by electronic signature; credit notes and correction invoices must cite the original SII record. B2B e-invoicing: under Law 18/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece), economic transactions must be issued as structured electronic invoices in interoperable formats (Facturae, UBL, CII) via AEAT-compatible platforms; the obligation becomes mandatory one year after the implementing Royal Decree for suppliers with annual turnover above EUR 8,000,000 and two years thereafter for all businesses; the implementing decree has been drafted and phased enforcement is expected from 2025/2026. AEAT does not operate a per-invoice central digital stamping or fiscal pre-clearance for B2B invoices; fiscal clearance is effected through SII electronic book submissions and the information exchange platform, while each e-invoice carries a hash-validated FRCE code from the delivering platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Two statutory routes can produce 0% VAT for a marine insurance surveyor. (1) Export-linked services: Article 22.1 LIVA zero-rates services directly relating to movable tangible property sent or transported outside the European Union, including services ancillary to physical exports (Articles 21 and 22 LIVA) provided before or immediately after the export operation; vessel hull and cargo damage surveying performed at Spanish ports qualifies when the inspected goods are destined for export or were imported temporarily and will be re-exported, and the insurer/Surveyor retains transport documentation. (2) B2B location rule for services to non-EU recipients: under Article 69.1 LIVA, services supplied to an entrepreneur or professional established outside the EU are deemed performed outside Spain and are accordingly not subject to Spanish VAT; this applies for survey services rendered to a foreign insurer or foreign shipowner without the need for a customs declaration. Conditions: the invoice must state the legal basis (e.g., 'Art. 22 LIVA – exento', or 'Art. 69.1 LIVA – no sujeto'), the recipient's foreign VAT/tax identification, proof of the recipient's establishment outside the EU, and the precise relation to the exported or to-be-exported goods; insurance claims-inspection services as such are not VAT-exempt under Article 20.16 LIVA (which exempts only insurance and reinsurance operations), so the zero-rating must always be substantiated by the export or non-establishment rule.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA – Documento Único Administrativo) endorsed with the definitive exit confirmation from the EU customs territory
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (or CMR) evidencing physical transport of the surveyed goods out of the EU, with port/airport stamps
Inward Remittance Certificate (justificante de cobro de la transferencia exterior) evidencing payment received from the non-resident insurer, reinsurer, or cargo owner
Marine insurance policy number, claims file reference, and survey engagement letter/contract demonstrating the surveyor's instructions from the foreign underwriter
Detailed survey report (draft and final), photographic evidence, signed surveyor certificate, and damage assessment documentation
Where temporary importation applies: ATA Carnet or temporary import declaration (Documento de Importación Temporal) proving the re-export obligation of the inspected goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT retaliatory review may cover up to four years retroactively and places the burden of proof on the taxpayer (Art. 105 LGT). AEAT cross-checks the DUA export confirmation, bill of lading exit dates, survey dates, insurer instruction chain, and the inward remittance certificate. A refused zero-rating results in a liquidation assessing output VAT at 21%, late-payment interest under Art. 26 LGT, and, if the taxpayer fails to file corrective VAT returns, penalties under Art. 191 LGT between 50% and 150% of the understated amount; the 150% upper band applies where false invoices, sham temporary-import/export cycles, or means involving unreachable persons are used. Uncollected export proceeds beyond the 180-day repatriation window are treated as unsupported exports and trigger clawback with apremio surcharge of 5-20% during the enforcement period. Fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 in any VAT period constitutes the criminal offense of tax fraud under Art. 305 of the Criminal Code, carrying imprisonment of one to five years, fines, and loss of public subsidies; the AEAT's annual audit plan for 2024-2025 particularly targets so-called 'surveyor cascades' where marine claim assessments are diverted to shell EU recipients to disguise export services. Refunds already obtained for claimed zero-rated exports are clawed back with interest from the date of the original refund.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the European System of Central Banks and the Single Supervisory Mechanism of the European Central Bank
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain, as a eurozone member state, maintains full and unrestricted currency convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) Articles 63-66 and Regulation (EC) No 1883/2005 on the application of certain provisions of EU law relating to capital movements. Profit remittances by resident or non-resident shareholders of a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada are freely permitted without prior administrative authorization, subject only to general anti-money laundering verification, the submission of corporate tax withholding certificates (e.g., Form 216 where applicable), and standard bank compliance screening. There are no exchange control approvals, no surrender requirements, and no restrictions on the use of euro-denominated or foreign currency accounts for trade-related settlements. Errors or materially misleading classifications of the purpose code in the B2B economic transaction registry may trigger statistical reporting obligations to the Balance of Payments Division of Banco de España, but do not constitute convertibility hurdles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. There is no obligation to surrender foreign currency earnings to the central bank or to any domestic financial institution. Exporters, including marine insurance surveying firms receiving fee income from underwriters outside Spain, may retain export receipts in foreign currency accounts or convert them to euros at their commercial discretion. Only statistical declaration duties apply under Royal Decree 1730/2022 (or successive balance-of-payments reporting regulations), requiring residents to report cross-border transactions exceeding €12,500 via the annual or monthly statistical forms (e.g., R-1, R-2) filed with Banco de España. No mandatory conversion or repatriation timeline exists.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-to-High for operational accounts and cross-border trade payments; Low for capital escrow or statutory capital deposit purposes. European-authorised Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) operating in Spain under the PSD2 passporting regime can provide multicurrency IBAN accounts, faster SWIFT-style transfers, and lower-cost clearing solutions for outbound trade disbursements, particularly those using the Wise (UK/SEPA/Belgium entity) platform. However, an EMI is not a credit institution and cannot legally hold statutory share capital or capital escrow balances as a qualifying Spanish deposit-taking entity. Additionally, the Bank of Spain Circular and AML regulations require that any account used for issuing share certificates or holding initial paid-in capital be with a Spanish-registered credit institution (deposit-taking bank). For operational fee income and marine survey disbursements, a PSD2-authorised EMI with a Spanish passport or an EEA branch may be viable, but the entity's hosting of funds is limited to e-money, not regulated deposit protection (FGD) unless the EMI has voluntary deposit protection arrangements. Foreign non-EEA EMIs not passported into Spain are not viable for receiving regulated capital injections or forex settlements with Spanish tax authorities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors is generally not mandated by Spanish AML law for standard entity onboarding, but most tier-1 Spanish banks trigger enhanced due diligence when the beneficial owner is a non-resident corporate entity. Under Law 10/2010 on Prevention of Money Laundering and Royal Decree 304/2014, banks must identify the legal representative and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO). Remote onboarding is permitted in Spain for low-risk and standard-risk entities, provided the following procedure is executed: (i) notarised power-of-attorney granted to the Spanish resident representative or legal counsel; (ii) apostilled and, if not in Spanish, legally translated certificates of incorporation, UBO registry extract, and passport copies; (iii) a live video-identification call with an authorised compliance officer of the bank; and (iv) verification of the source of funds via prior bank statements or a solicitor's escrow confirmation. For a newly formed SL without Spanish directors, principal-tier banks such as BBVA and CaixaBank will typically condition account opening on the physical appearance of the sole director, or at least a local notary visit, unless the bank's remote onboarding platform is active for corporate clients. Therefore, to avoid rejection, we recommend designating a Spanish resident manager or legal representative for the physical interview; otherwise remote onboarding with deep KYC files is only viable at entity-onboarding platforms (e.g., CaixaBank Sign, BBVA Contigo) for entities with a proven track record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate shareholder owning ultimate beneficial ownership through a non-transparent offshore jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial ownership registry certificate (e.g., Registro de Titularidad Real) issued by the Spanish Notarial Registry; a tax residence certificate of the parent company; consolidated organisational chart evidencing all intermediate shareholders; audited financial statements and bank reference letters from the parent's main banker in the parent's jurisdiction; sworn statutory declaration identifying natural-person UBOs; and, if applicable, an independent legal opinion confirming that the offshore entity is not shell but actively trading with substantive operations in a jurisdiction with adequate AML standards.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial paid-in capital (minimum €3,000,000 in some standard banks if they demand a higher escrow, or the legally optional smaller registered capital for SL of €3,000 to €30,000)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank account statements of the contributing shareholders for the preceding 12 months evidencing a traceable origin of salary, dividends, sale of assets, or family accumulation; a notarised capital contribution agreement (Escritura de Aportación); an auditor's or chartered accountant's report confirming that funds originate from a lawful and declared income stream; tax returns (e.g., Spanish Form 720 or foreign equivalent) relating to the funds; and an unfolding narrative memo explaining the economic rationale for the capital injection into a marine insurance surveyor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk marine casualty claims involving cargo or vessel hull losses in sanctioned waters or with flagged vessels from restricted territories
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full survey report with GPS coordinates and vessel tracking records (AIS data) proving the location of the survey; contractual clauses confirming that the Spanish SL is only performing non-claim-adjustment inspection services, not acting as a claims settlement agent; OVID or shipping registry verification of the vessel's compliance; export/import control screening of the counterparty and beneficial owner against EU consolidated sanctions lists; and a legal compliance certificate from the in-house or external sanctions officer confirming that no prohibited activity under EU Regulations 833/2014 and 269/2014 is present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commingling of corporate funds with private or surveyor's personal accounts due to the entity's small capital and single-owner structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate bank account statements immediately after incorporation and after first inbound payments; meticulously maintained shareholder loan agreements (contrato préstamo socios); a resolution of the sole shareholder approving transactions; and an external accounting record showing clear separation between operational and treasury flows. To defend against AML reclassification, the entity should maintain a compliance manual and, if the volume of cross-border transactions exceeds €50,000 per month, appoint an external compliance consultant to audit the transaction ledger.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For an SL composed as a marine insurance surveyor, the inbound capital injection from a non-resident shareholder is routed via SWIFT MT103/ISO 20022 pain.001 using the following protocol: (1) the shareholder initiates a cross-border wire to the SL's euro-denominated account in Spain with the bank's BIC/SWIFT (e.g., BBVAESMMXXX) and the account IBAN based on ES + check digits + National Bank Code + 20 digits; (2) in the wire instruction, the registry must include the proper economic purpose code: in Spain, banks use the Balance of Payments statistical form A-1 for capital contributions; the purpose declaration should be 'Aportación de capital social' (capital contribution) with code E26 under the Banco de España's B2B statistical reporting; (3) the bank will require a notarised copy of the public deed of incorporation (escritura pública) and proof of registration of the SL at the Mercantile Registry, to map the inbound amount to the share capital increase in the corporate records; (4) if the contribution exceeds €10,000 from a related foreign company, Spanish anti-money laundering regulations require execution of the official 'Declaración de Movimientos de Medios de Pago' (Form S1) only if cash transported; for electronic transfers, just the regular AML verification of the sender; (5) after the funds are credited, the accounting of the share premium or paid-in capital must be reported within one month to the commercial registry if the capital increase is formalised; a special rule applies where the SL is using the capital to purchase a marine survey office in Spain, as the bank may request the purchase contract and tax paid on stamp duty (AJD) in order to disburse the funds. For non-resident direct investment, no prior foreign investment authorisation is required under Royal Decree 664/1999, but the investment must be recorded with the Bank of Spain's Foreign Investment Registry via the electronic form depending on the fiscal year aggregate threshold (generally above €3,005,000).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade-related disbursements by a Spanish marine insurance surveyor (e.g., paying subcontracted loss adjusters overseas, buying specialised survey equipment, paying dry-dock inspection fees for a vessel in a foreign port, or reimbursing external cargo experts), the optimal clearing rails are: (i) SWIFT MT103 direct correspondent transfer between the Spanish bank and the beneficiary bank in the third country; (ii) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) using IBAN and BIC for euro payments within the SEPA zone, with a T+1 settlement and no withholding tax; (iii) Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) opened via a Spanish issuing bank, advisable when the surveyor is paying a foreign technology vendor or subcontractor above €100,000 and wants documentary protection via LC clauses (shipment inspection reports, invoice, receipt); (iv) for cross-border euro payments outside SEPA, use SWIFT MT103 with the reason for payment code (e.g., 'Insurance surveys and consultancy' using UN/EDIFACT codes Dolgood98, or D30 for professional services). The firm must include in each outgoing wire the Spanish corporate tax identification (NIF) and, if the payment is subject to Spanish withholding tax, the declaration of IRNR (Form 216) for non-resident recipients; for services linked to maritime insurance risk, professional service fees are generally not subject to Spanish corporate income tax on the non-resident unless the non-resident has a permanent establishment in Spain. For trade payments to offshore (non-EEA) beneficiaries, the bank's anti-financial crime committee will request the invoice/contract evidencing freight risk or survey work and may require a Certificate of Residence or W-8BEN-E / W-8IMY for US counterparties, and additionally a sanctions screening of the vessel's IMO number if the payment is for marine services in third-party territorial waters.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (Cobertura a plazo) between EUR and USD/GBP/JPY/CHF, permitted for a maximum tenor of 12 months without extra regulatory authorisation under Banco de España rules, requiring proof of underlying commercial exposure from marine survey invoice commitments.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market currencies (e.g., BRL, MXN, ARS) where the convertibility of the underlying currency is restricted and physical exchange cannot be executed onshore; Spanish credit institutions active in Latin American markets offer NDF contracts incident to trade transactions, but these are only permissible for hedging real exposure from fees receivable from underwriters in these countries, not for speculative positions.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for converting a foreign currency loan or a long-term financial lease into EUR, used if the SL finances a marine laboratory via a USD-denominated or CHF-denominated facility; the swap can be executed directly with the lending bank or a broker, subject to the EMIR clearing obligation for derivatives if the bank is considered a financial counterparty and the notional exceeds €1.5 billion per clearing threshold.

FX options (European-style vanilla puts/calls) as structured hedges embedded in an overseas invoice or fee collection facility, permissible if executed via a Spanish MiFID II licensed investment firm and with suitability testing of the entity as a professional counterparty; speculative FX trading is not prohibited but is not recommended for a standard SL and will be scrutinised by the bank's income attribution rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved within six months after the financial year-end and deposited within one month after approval. For a 31 December year-end, typical deposit deadline is 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit may cause closure of the company registry sheet after one year from the end of the filing period, administrative fines generally ranging from approximately EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, and potential director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Electronic accounting books must generally be legalized within four months after the financial year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the typical deadline is 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted legalization may impair evidentiary value, trigger inspection or enforcement exposure, and support administrative sanctions for accounting and corporate-law non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first 25 calendar days after six months from the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the typical filing window is 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger fixed or percentage-based penalties, late-payment interest, and collection surcharges. Unpaid tax may be subject to enforcement proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership declaration accompanying the annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with the annual accounts filing, with updates required when beneficial ownership information changes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or missing beneficial ownership information may cause filing rejection, registry compliance issues, and administrative or anti-money-laundering sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business activity tax compliance review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency or competent local authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No universal annual renewal applies. The company must review its registration and exemption status annually and file any required census or activity changes within the applicable statutory period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register or report activity changes may result in tax assessments, interest, surcharges, and penalties. Entities with net turnover below EUR 1 million are generally exempt from paying Spanish Economic Activities Tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets above EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover above EUR 5.7 million, or average employees above 50. Audit may also be mandatory under sector-specific rules, group-accounting rules, public-interest requirements, grants, or court or shareholder appointment.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the Spanish General Accounting Plan. IFRS is generally relevant for consolidated accounts of qualifying groups and may apply to regulated or listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain has no separate annual confirmation filing solely for shareholding transfers. The company must maintain current beneficial ownership information, update it when ownership or control changes, and submit the applicable beneficial ownership declaration with the annual accounts filing. Share transfers must also be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in corporate documentation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Contracts with the Sole Shareholder, if applicable
Beneficial ownership records and supporting identification documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 325-975 per year, excluding mail handling, tax representation, and additional corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 1,500-5,000 for a small non-complex Spanish SL requiring a statutory audit; no audit fee applies where the company is not subject to mandatory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created qualifying start-ups on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable income in the first two profitable years; R&D tax credits of 25% to 42%; international double taxation relief and participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carryforward, subject to annual offset limitations under Spanish LIS Art. 26)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) - Corporate Income Tax Return, filed electronically through the AEAT Sede Electrónica (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (per fiscal year; short-period returns for incorporation, liquidation or tax period change)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal year close; for a calendar-year entity, the filing window runs from 1 July to 25 July of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer's Spanish tax identification number; a resident Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada uses NIF starting with 'B' (e.g. B12345670).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies operating through a Spanish permanent establishment must obtain an NIF through Form 036/037 and enter that NIF here; non-resident entities without a permanent establishment must not use Modelo 200 but instead file Modelo 210 for non-resident income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates in DD/MM/YYYY format.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Spanish permanent establishment, report the fiscal year adopted by the foreign head office; for a non-resident without a permanent establishment, use the natural year and Modelo 210.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss before tax derived from the statutory income statement prepared under Spanish GAAP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Spanish permanent establishment, include only profit attributable to the permanent establishment under Spanish attribution rules; do not consolidate non-resident shareholders' income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after adjustments for tax-exempt income, use of prior-year loss carryforwards, tax credits and withholding credits; final corporate income tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a permanent establishment, apply the 25% rate on the attributed taxable base; non-resident investors claiming treaty relief on income from the permanent establishment should use the corresponding Modelo 210 procedure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior notification: surcharges of 10% of tax due if filed within 3 months after deadline, 15% if within 6 months, and 20% if within 12 months; after 12 months surcharge remains 20% with late-payment interest; if no tax is due, fixed penalty of EUR 200 applies; post-inspection penalties may range from 50% to 150% of the tax loss.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% (Spanish domestic IRNR rate on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders without a permanent establishment)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must present a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the competent foreign tax authority to the Spanish paying entity before payment, or file Form 210 to claim a refund of excess withholding; EU/Austrian treaty situations may use the Form 296 procedure for reduced source-country withholding; attribution of treaty benefits requires genuine economic substance and beneficial ownership under the Principal Purpose Test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic IRNR withholding: 19% for interest and 19% for most capital-yield-based income; royalties and similar income often fall under the general 25% IRNR rate when not covered by preferential catalogue provisions. Under most Spanish double tax treaties, the withholding cap is 10% for interest and 10% for royalties (e.g. Spain-China and Spain-US treaties); a treaty condition may reduce to 5% for certain intercompany loans or licence contracts.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 aggregate related-party transactions per year for mandatory Local File; Master File is required when the consolidated group turnover exceeds EUR 12,000,000; entities with turnover below EUR 10,000,000 are generally exempt from documentation, but must still apply the arm's length principle.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); instead, a Spanish SL must demonstrate genuine economic activity through GAAR (LGT Art. 15), anti-abuse clauses, CFC rules and the OECD BEPS Principal Purpose Test in order to access treaty benefits. For marine insurance surveyor operations, professional staff, physical claim-inspection activity, and adequate local record-keeping will evidence substantive commercial purpose.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Criminal Tax Fraud (Defraudación tributaria)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally issuing false marine cargo survey reports to under-report Spanish corporate revenue, overstating deductible expenses, or concealing claims-settlement income to reduce the Spanish income tax payable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish Criminal Code (Ley Orgánica 10/1995, Art. 305): imprisonment for 1 to 5 years plus a fine of six to twelve months where the evaded amount exceeds EUR 120,000; aggravated regime (Art. 305 bis) for amounts above EUR 600,000 applies imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and a fine of double to sixfold the defrauded amount. Administrative penalty under LGT can be imposed at 50% to 150% of the tax deficiency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who knowingly cause or conceal the evasion are personally criminally liable; the corporate veil may be pierced for civil restitution; travel bans, asset seizures and imprisonment are available penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating or using an SL with no real business activity, employees, premises or records, solely to route marine survey fees through a tax-beneficial structure, invoice for falsified services or nominee shareholders/directors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR (LGT Art. 15) allows AEAT to annul the tax effect of the artificial scheme and reassess tax with late-payment interest; the entity will be denied treaty benefits under BEPS PPT; administrative fines for abusive structures may reach 150% of the tax loss; if the entity becomes insolvent, unpaid tax may be collected from shareholders or group companies under joint and several liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who cause or participate in the sham arrangement may be jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax (LGT Art. 42.2); in cases involving tax evasion above EUR 120,000, criminal prosecution with imprisonment and personal fine is possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner of a policyholder or corporate claimant, failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) with SEPBLAC, or facilitating fraudulent insurance claim payments used for money laundering in the marine cargo surveying business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 10/2010 on AML: serious violations carry fines of EUR 60,001 to EUR 1,500,000; very serious violations may lead to entity dissolution; criminal money-laundering under Criminal Code Art. 301 can result in imprisonment from 6 months to 6 years and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible compliance officer or director may be personally fined; courts may order travel bans, forfeiture of assets and professional disqualification of up to 10 years; if the entity is used as a laundering vehicle, the director can also be prosecuted as an accomplice.
